correctness.rationale: The only positive-change order has the marked clique vertex first globally and the centre first among its star. Its probability is 1/[(k+m+1)(k+1)]. The leaves replace the centre, contributing k−1 extra accepts; if the centre instead blocks the clique vertex, a different clique vertex replaces it for m≥2. Moving this mass from 2 to k+1 gives the law. For m=1 the mean difference of the larger star versus the smaller star plus an isolate is −2/[(k+1)(k+2)]. Independent exhaustive set-based permutation counting of 1, 2, 8, 64 and 1024 graphs tested 0, 1, 12, 192 and 5120 nonedges; positive counts were 0, 0, 0, 0, 240, all gains 8/120. The full relabelling orbits of the displayed representatives are disjoint, of sizes 60, 120, 60, and exhaust the positives; their respective old/new numerators over 120 are (320,328), (296,304), (304,312). The empty graph trivially contributes no augmentation.
residual_risks: The exhaustive check is only through order five; the all-parameter formula uses the separate analytic coupling.
